title: The stitch the body keeps
note: Al-Zahrawi drew two hundred surgical instruments and introduced dissolving sutures still used today.

research.quotes: heroes.html#f-medicine: 'Abu al-Qasim al-Zahrawi, about 936 to 1013, Madinat al-Zahra, near Cordoba.' 'al-Tasrif... Around two hundred of them, scalpels, forceps, hooks, bone saws... illustrated precisely enough that a surgeon far away could have them made.' 'a surgeon who does not know anatomy has no business holding a blade.' 'sutures of catgut, thread made from animal intestine, which the body slowly and safely absorbs... Dissolving stitches still work on his principle today.'
research.retell: A surgeon named Al-Zahrawi drew about two hundred surgical tools so precisely that other surgeons could copy them, and he also invented dissolving stitches that surgeons still use today.

lines.text: Your surgeon's tools were drawn in 1000
lines.sub: drawn precisely enough for surgeons to copy
a surgeon named Abu al-Qasim al-Zahrawi

lines.text: He draws each tool, precise enough to copy
Centuries later, the shapes sit on a tray
He stitches wounds with thread of catgut
The body slowly absorbs the thread itself
Old thread had to be cut back out
lines.sub: his stitches leave with no second cut

lines.text: Dissolving stitches work on his principle
He drew around two hundred instruments
